facts.statement: Require IER bits 0-3 to enable or disable Received Data THRE Receiver Line Status and Modem Status interrupt generation.
facts.quote: This register allows enabling and disabling interrupt generation by the UART.

facts.statement: IER bit 0 is Received Data available interrupt with 0 disabled and 1 enabled.
facts.quote:
0 RW Received Data available interrupt
 ‘0’ – disabled
 ‘1’ – enabled

facts.statement: IER bit 1 is Transmitter Holding Register empty interrupt with 0 disabled and 1 enabled.
facts.quote:
1 RW Transmitter Holding Register empty interrupt
 ‘0’ – disabled
 ‘1’ – enabled

facts.statement: IER bit 2 is Receiver Line Status Interrupt with 0 disabled and 1 enabled.
facts.quote:
2 RW Receiver Line Status Interrupt
 ‘0’ – disabled
 ‘1’ – enabled

facts.statement: IER bit 3 is Modem Status Interrupt with 0 disabled and 1 enabled.
facts.quote:
3 RW Modem Status Interrupt
 ‘0’ – disabled
 ‘1’ – enabled

facts.statement: IER is at bus address 1 width 8 access RW for Enable Mask interrupts.
Addresses 0-1 cannot be accessed when DLAB is 1 so DLAB must be 0 to access IER at address 1.
facts.quote: At this time the above registers at addresses 0-1 can’t be accessed.

facts.statement: Upon reset all interrupts are disabled in the Interrupt Enable Register.
facts.quote: All interrupts are disabled in the Interrupt Enable Register.

facts.statement: Enable desired interrupts by setting appropriate bits in the Interrupt Enable register.
facts.quote: Enable desired interrupts by setting appropriate bits in the Interrupt Enable

facts.statement: IIR bit 0 reports pending as 0 and no pending as 1.
facts.quote: Bit 0 indicates that an interrupt is pending when it’s logic ‘0’. When it’s ‘1’ – no interrupt

facts.statement: IIR retrieves the current highest priority pending interrupt.
facts.quote: The IIR enables the programmer to retrieve what is the current highest priority pending

facts.statement: IIR reset value is C1h implying bit0 1 no pending at reset.
